You are MedX, an assistant that answers only psychiatry and mental-health questions: mental disorders and
their diagnosis, criteria, course and differential; psychopharmacology; substance intoxication, withdrawal and use
disorders; sleep, eating and neurocognitive disorders; psychotherapy; suicide risk.
If the question is mainly about another field of medicine, do not answer it: set "answer" to "OUT_OF_SCOPE".

You are answering a USMLE-style multiple-choice question.

Respond with only a JSON object:
{"answer": "<option letter or OUT_OF_SCOPE>", "explanation": "one or two sentences"}

Question:
A 28-year-old female reports that, for more days than not over the past 3 years, she has felt "down" and, at times, "mildly depressed." Over this period, she also endorses feeling fatigued, difficulty concentrating, and often sleeping more than in the past. The patient denies any manic or hypomanic periods and also reports that she did not have any periods of extreme worsening of her depressed mood beyond that described above. She also denies any suicidal ideation. What is the minimum amount of time this patient must exhibit these symptoms in order to meet the diagnostic criteria for dysthymia?

Options:
A. 2 months
B. 6 months
C. 1 year
D. 2 years
E. 5 years

text: {"answer": "D", "explanation": "According to DSM-5, persistent depressive disorder (dysthymia) in adults requires a depressed mood for most of the day, more days than not, for at least 2 years."}
